text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kuwait's Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah to discuss Gulf security with U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen. Cohen is scheduled to arrive in Kuwait from Saudi Arabia later on Sunday.
- Acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah says there will be no parliament dissolution nor a government reshuffle.

- Opposition parliamentrian Abdullah al-Naibari flies to Boston today for medical treatment after surviving an assassination attempt earlier in June. Kuwait has arrested five people in connection with the attempt.
- Parliament discussed security and foreign affairs issues in a closed session o Saturday.
- Kuwait to take part in a meeting of Gulf Arab states' electricity officials.
- Volume of trade between Turkey and Kuwait amounted to $45.4 million in 1996, Turkish embassy official says.
- Sheikh Sabah says Kuwait to restore soon ties with countries which supported Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait.

- Kuwait's ambassador to Tunisia discussed the issue of Kuwaiti POWs with Tunisian Foreign Minister Abderrahim Zouari. About 600 Kuwaitis are believed to be held in Iraq since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.
- More than 13,000 families received aid during 1996, family welfare official says.
